explain.say: Flying fish do not flap, but they glide like paper planes. It is a getaway trick: leaping into the air lets them escape tuna, dolphins and other fast hunters below.

explain.say: A flying fish swims fast towards the surface, bursts out and spreads its huge pectoral fins like wings. Some kinds spread their pelvic fins too, like a second, smaller pair.

explain.say: In the air, the spread fins make lift to balance the fish's weight while drag slowly slows it. By dipping its tail back in for another push, a flying fish can string glides together; one was filmed staying up for 45 seconds.

faq.a: Not by flapping. They glide on their stiff, outspread pectoral fins, which work like the wings of a glider, after building up speed in the water.
asks: Can flying fish flap their fins?

faq.q: Why do flying fish leave the water?
faq.a: Mainly to escape predators such as tuna, mackerel and dolphins. A hunter chasing underwater suddenly loses sight of its prey as it sails away through the air.
asks: Why do fish jump out of the sea?

faq.q: How far can flying fish glide?
faq.a: A single glide is often around 50 metres and can reach about 200. By dipping the tail back in and taxiing again, a flying fish can cover around 400 metres in a series of glides.
asks: How long can a flying fish stay in the air?
What is the longest flying fish flight?

faq.q: How fast do flying fish go before they glide?
faq.a: They burst from the water at more than 50 kilometres per hour, and the tail beating against the surface gives them the final burst of speed for take-off.
asks: How do flying fish take off?

faq.a: They fold their fins and drop back into the sea, or dip the tail into the water and beat it again to launch another glide without fully landing.
asks: What happens when a flying fish comes down?
Do flying fish glide more than once?

facts: A flying fish filmed off Japan in 2008 stayed in the air for about 45 seconds.
Flying fish beat their tails very rapidly against the surface, up to about 70 times a second, while taxiing.

wrong.1: The fins are held stiff for gliding; they do not flap.
wrong.2: Wind can help a glide, but the take-off is powered by the tail.

quiz.say: Why do flying fish glide out of the water?
quiz.show: Why do flying fish glide out of the water?
quiz.why: Leaving the water suddenly makes them vanish from hunters such as tuna and dolphins.

wrong.1: Flying fish feed on plankton in the water, not insects in the air.
wrong.2: Fish do not need to dry their fins.
